rules.sentence: The osteoid matrix produced by tumor cells must be identified somewhere in the lesion, even if only in a minuscule amount.[24]
Histologically, COS is composed of cells that are spindle to polyhedral in shape with variable nuclei and numerous mitotic figures.[24]
Histologically, telangiectatic osteosarcoma is characterized by numerous blood-filled sinusoids with septations containing cells with nuclear pleomorphism and numerous mitotic figures.[24]
The lesional tissue is also observed permeating into the surrounding marrow or cortex.[24]
